To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
objective ratings of multiple relationship skills are associated with initial levels of marital satisfaction and with subsequent rates of change in marital satisfaction.

objective ratings of five relationship skills were associated with initial and change in marital satisfaction over three years, with sexual intimacy and communication/conflict skills predicting change in marital satisfaction for husbands and wives, respectively.
objective ratings of relationship skills in five domains are associated with initial levels of marital satisfaction and with subsequent rates of change in marital satisfaction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether marital satisfaction is associated with the quality of a couple's relationship.
the role of multiple dyadic skills in marital satisfaction.
how couples' relational skills are associated with marital satisfaction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the most important predictor of marital satisfaction is how well you and your spouse communicate and manage conflict in the marriage.
the most important predictor of marital satisfaction is a couple’s ability to communicate effectively and to resolve conflicts constructively.
the results of this study support the notion that the quality of the marital relationship is a function of multiple dyadic skills.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the more a couple can learn to effectively manage conflict, the more likely they are to experience greater marital satisfaction over time.
marital satisfaction trajectories are predicted by multiple dyadic behaviors.
the quality of the relationship is the most important determinant of marital satisfaction and stability.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is important to assess relationship skills in multiple domains and to consider the impact of these domains on marital outcomes.

the relationship skills of husbands and wives are differentially associated with marital satisfaction trajectories, suggesting the need to assess and intervene on multiple relationship behaviors in order to promote healthy marriages.
